children: all hit fresh 52-week highs by afternoon trading on Thursday as artificial intelligence and agentic adoption prompt a greater need for cybersecurity.

CrowdStrike shares inched up 0.5% while Rubrik increased 1.5%, with both on track to close at all-time highs. Okta edged up 1.2%, putting it on track to close at its highest value since December 2021. SentinelOne
increased 3% as it's on track to close at its highest point since December 2024.

Okta focuses on identity management, which has become crucial with the rise of agents. These agents can operate as a type of virtual employee that requires its own verifiable digital identity separate from the human users who enable them.
"So I feel like the luckiest guy in the world leading this company at this time," said Okta co-founder and CEO Todd McKinnon during an
last week. "We're at exactly the perfect moment. We have to bring visibility and control to this industry right now."
Okta's most recent earnings results showed its near-term subscription backlog increasing by 14%, while its free cash flow hit $227M.
Rubrik co-founder and CEO Bipul Sinha highlighted the growing importance of cybersecurity measures, especially runtime security, during a Goldman Sachs conference last month.
Hugging Face is these agents, to get to a goal, actually circumvented the guardrails that were built for them," he
. "So you need to understand the intent of the agent and check the intent on every interaction of the agent to be able to stop the agentic action on runtime at the point of action."
According to PwC, which released its 2027 Global Digital Insights Survey on Thursday, 84% of security and finance leaders expect cyber budgets to increase.

"As organisations race to capture the value of AI, cyber resilience needs to become a business capability, embedded in C-suite decision-making from the outset," said Avinash Rajeev, Global Cyber, Data & Tech Risk Leader at PwC US. "The survey finds many organisations are still under-prepared for a rapidly evolving cyber landscape, and organisations that get this right will be better positioned to innovate with confidence while continuing to operate through disruption."

A Gartner forecast from earlier this year also indicated enterprises are not spending enough on cybersecurity. It found that while enterprises on a global scale are expected to increase spending on AI initiatives by 44% year over year in 2026, cybersecurity spending is only expected to increase by 13.3%.
